# Real debark stderr, captured against a real binary. Not hand-written.
#
# Binary:   debark dev (community), commit 94612f558cd26fa57d6c0185956ff153c5162833,
#           built 2026-09-06T22:20:14Z, go1.26.0, windows/amd64 — the same commit
#           docs/dev/cli-surface.md was verified against.
# Captured: 2026-09-06, from a scratch directory, redirecting stderr to a file.
# Encoding: LF line endings exactly as the binary wrote them. Byte-exact, with
#           one exception noted below.
#
# `build` and `install` were never run. Every `build` sample below is a cobra
# flag-validation failure, which happens before RunE and therefore before any
# work: no network, no container, no bundle directory.
#
# Format: <file> TAB <exit code> TAB <the invocation that produced it>
# Lines beginning with # are comments. errors_test.go reads this file.
#
# Redaction: usage-verify-missing-bundle.stderr had the capturing directory's
# absolute path in it (it names the resolved bundle path twice). The session
# temp prefix was replaced with C:\Users\operator\bundles. Nothing else in any
# sample was edited.
#
# The two zero-byte samples are the point of the exercise, not an accident:
# `verify` renders its --json report and then returns a SILENCED error, exactly
# as `build` does (cli-surface.md C1). Exit 4, and not one byte on stderr.

usage-verify-missing-bundle.stderr		1	debark verify ./no-such-bundle --json

usage-doctor-no-target.stderr			1	debark doctor --json
usage-build-no-target.stderr			1	debark build --json

usage-inspect-no-args.stderr			1	debark inspect --json
